meta.note: Northern Ireland's domestic rating rules, for Belfast (etl/northern_ireland.py, apps/web RatesBill). Homes pay rates, not council tax: capital value times the district and regional rates. Read from nidirect and the Department for Communities on 9 October 2026.

sources.title: The Rates (Maximum Capital Value) (Amendment) Regulations (Northern Ireland) 2009 (SR 2009/77)
District council (NI) rate statistics 2026/2027, circular LG 08/2026, introduction (Department for Communities)

capital_value_cap.note: "The maximum capital valuation for a domestic property is £400,000": value above it is disregarded. Set by SR 2007/184, lowered from £500,000 by SR 2009/77 from 1 April 2009. A 2025 review proposed £485,000; nothing has changed for 2026-27.

valuation_date.note: Capital value is "based on property values on 1 January 2005" (Rates (Northern Ireland) Order 1977, Schedule 12, paragraph 7(4)). No new valuation of homes has been set.

lone_pensioner_allowance.note: 20 per cent off for someone aged 70 or over who lives alone; not means tested; by application (Land & Property Services, or the Housing Executive for its tenants).

instalments.note: "You can make one payment for the full amount or spread payments over ten months."

balanced_budget.note: Local Government Finance Act (Northern Ireland) 2011, section 3: each year a council estimates its income and spending and fixes the amount to be raised by rates. Funding must equal spending to £1,000.
